questions.q: What four things does this lesson recommend covering in a five-minute capstone presentation?
options: Company history, team bios, funding, and roadmap
The model, the deployment, the security, and the monitoring
Only the final invoice from Azure
A full line-by-line code review
questions.explain: The recommended walkthrough covers the model deployed, the live deployment itself, one working security control, and the monitoring setup.

questions.q: Why does naming a specific limitation work better than claiming the system is flawless?
options: It makes the presentation shorter
Limitations are required by Azure's terms of service
It has no real effect either way
It shows you understand what you'd still need to build, not just what you finished
questions.explain: A named, specific limitation (like needing autoscaling for concurrent load) demonstrates real understanding of the system, which survives follow-up questions better than a claim of perfection.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend deleting the capstone deployment after presenting it?
options: A managed-compute deployment bills by the hour whether or not it's being used
Azure requires all deployments to be deleted within 24 hours
Deleting it is required to receive a certificate
It has no effect on billing either way
questions.explain: Managed-compute deployments bill by the hour regardless of usage, so deleting the deployment (or letting a shared-quota timer expire) after capturing proof avoids ongoing cost.
